raw_response:
I've been working this land for 40 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. My son is in the city now, so most of the fieldwork falls on me, and I'm not as strong as I used to be. I try not to change things too much — what worked before will work again.

For wheat, I plant after the maize comes off in early October. I'll plough first to turn under the stubble properly. I use whatever improved variety the seed store in town has been pushing the last few years — something that handles our dry conditions. I water before sowing to get good germination, then again before it gets cold, then at jointing, then at heading. That's what my father did, that's what I do. Four waterings. I put compound fertilizer down before planting, then urea in spring when things green up. I'll spray twice — once for weeds early, once for aphids when they show up.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. I use hybrid seed — everybody does now, the yields are better. I do rotary tillage — quicker, and I need to get seed in fast. I put fertilizer down with planting and topdress once when the plants are knee-high. Rain in summer is hit or miss, so I'll water twice if it looks dry. I spray once for corn borer, sometimes twice if it's bad.

I'm not changing much this year. The land knows me and I know the land.
